title: TRIGONOMETRIC LIMITS — First-Principle Substitution Method (x → a type problems)
notes:
📘 TOPIC: Evaluating limits of the form lim(x→θ) [x·f(θ) − θ·f(x)] / (x−θ), and lim(x→a) [f(x)−f(a)]/(x−a), where f is a trigonometric function (sin, cos, tan, cot, sec, cosec).

These all reduce to 0/0 on direct substitution and are solved using the SUBSTITUTION METHOD combined with SUM-TO-PRODUCT identities.

🔑 THE CORE TECHNIQUE (used in every problem below): STEP 1 — Let x = θ + h (or x = a + h), so that as x→θ (or x→a), h→0, and x−θ = h.

STEP 2 — Substitute into the expression and split into two separate limit terms.

STEP 3 — Apply a sum-to-product trigonometric identity to convert the difference of two trig functions into a product involving sin(h/2) or similar.

STEP 4 — Use the standard result lim(h→0) sin(h/2)/(h/2) = 1 to evaluate.

📐 SUM-TO-PRODUCT IDENTITIES NEEDED: sinA − sinB = 2·cos((A+B)/2)·sin((A−B)/2)  |  cosA − cosB = −2·sin((A+B)/2)·sin((A−B)/2)  |  tanA − tanB = sin(A−B)/(cosA·cosB)  |  cotA − cotB = sin(B−A)/(sinA·sinB)  |  secA − secB = (cosB−cosA)/(cosA·cosB)  |  cosecA − cosecB = (sinB−sinA)/(sinA·sinB)
═══════════ PROBLEM 1: lim(x→θ) [x·sinθ − θ·sinx] / (x−θ) ═══════════
Step 1: Let x − θ = h, so h→0 as x→θ, i.e., x = θ+h.
Step 2: Rewrite the limit: lim(h→0) [(θ+h)sinθ − θ·sin(θ+h)] / h
Step 3: Expand the numerator: θsinθ + h·sinθ − θ·sin(θ+h)
Step 4: Group terms: = θ[sinθ − sin(θ+h)] + h·sinθ
Step 5: Split into two limits: lim(h→0) θ·[sinθ−sin(θ+h)]/h + lim(h→0) sinθ
Step 6: Apply identity sinA−sinB = 2cos((A+B)/2)sin((A−B)/2) with A=θ, B=θ+h: sinθ−sin(θ+h) = −2·cos((2θ+h)/2)·sin(h/2)
Step 7: Substitute: lim(h→0) θ·[−2cos((2θ+h)/2)·sin(h/2)]/h = lim(h→0) −θ·cos((2θ+h)/2)·[sin(h/2)/(h/2)]
Step 8: As h→0: sin(h/2)/(h/2) → 1, and cos((2θ+h)/2) → cosθ
Step 9: This term becomes: −θ·cosθ·1 = −θcosθ
Step 10: Add back the second part (sinθ): Total = −θcosθ + sinθ
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→θ) [x·sinθ − θ·sinx]/(x−θ) = sinθ − θ·cosθ
═══════════ PROBLEM 2: lim(x→θ) [x·cosθ − θ·cosx] / (x−θ) ═══════════
Step 1: Let x = θ+h, so h→0 as x→θ.
Step 2: lim(h→0) [(θ+h)cosθ − θcos(θ+h)]/h
Step 3: Expand: θcosθ + h·cosθ − θ·cos(θ+h)
Step 4: Group: = θ[cosθ − cos(θ+h)] + h·cosθ
Step 5: Apply identity cosA−cosB = −2sin((A+B)/2)sin((A−B)/2): cosθ−cos(θ+h) = 2·sin((2θ+h)/2)·sin(h/2)
Step 6: θ[cosθ−cos(θ+h)]/h = θ·2·sin((2θ+h)/2)·sin(h/2)/h = θ·sin((2θ+h)/2)·[sin(h/2)/(h/2)]
Step 7: As h→0: sin(h/2)/(h/2)→1, sin((2θ+h)/2)→sinθ. This term → θ·sinθ
Step 8: Add the second part (cosθ): Total = θsinθ + cosθ
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→θ) [x·cosθ − θ·cosx]/(x−θ) = cosθ + θ·sinθ
═══════════ PROBLEM 3: lim(x→θ) [x·tanθ − θ·tanx] / (x−θ) ═══════════
Step 1: Let x = θ+h, so h→0 as x→θ.
Step 2: lim(h→0) [(θ+h)tanθ − θtan(θ+h)]/h = lim(h→0) θ[tanθ−tan(θ+h)]/h + tanθ
Step 3: Apply identity tanA−tanB = sin(A−B)/(cosA·cosB): tanθ−tan(θ+h) = sin(θ−(θ+h))/[cosθ·cos(θ+h)] = sin(−h)/[cosθcos(θ+h)] = −sinh/[cosθcos(θ+h)]
Step 4: θ[tanθ−tan(θ+h)]/h = −θ·[sinh/h]/[cosθ·cos(θ+h)]
Step 5: As h→0: sinh/h→1, cos(θ+h)→cosθ. This term → −θ/[cosθ·cosθ] = −θ·sec²θ
Step 6: Add tanθ: Total = tanθ − θ·sec²θ
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→θ) [x·tanθ − θ·tanx]/(x−θ) = tanθ − θ·sec²θ
═══════════ PROBLEM 4: lim(x→θ) [x·cosecθ − θ·cosecx] / (x−θ) ═══════════
Step 1: Let x = θ+h, so h→0 as x→θ.
Step 2: lim(h→0) [(θ+h)cosecθ − θcosec(θ+h)]/h = lim(h→0) θ[cosecθ−cosec(θ+h)]/h + cosecθ
Step 3: Apply identity cosecA−cosecB = [sinB−sinA]/(sinA·sinB): cosecθ−cosec(θ+h) = [sin(θ+h)−sinθ]/[sinθ·sin(θ+h)]
Step 4: Apply sinA−sinB identity to the numerator: sin(θ+h)−sinθ = 2·cos((2θ+h)/2)·sin(h/2)
Step 5: θ[cosecθ−cosec(θ+h)]/h = θ·2cos((2θ+h)/2)·sin(h/2) / [h·sinθ·sin(θ+h)] = θ·cos((2θ+h)/2)·[sin(h/2)/(h/2)] / [sinθ·sin(θ+h)]
Step 6: As h→0: this term → θ·cosθ / [sinθ·sinθ] = θ·cosθ/sin²θ
Step 7: Add cosecθ = 1/sinθ: Total = θcosθ/sin²θ + 1/sinθ = [θcosθ + sinθ]/sin²θ
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→θ) [x·cosecθ − θ·cosecx]/(x−θ) = (sinθ + θ·cosθ)/sin²θ  = cosecθ·(1 + θ·cotθ)
═══════════ PROBLEM 5: lim(x→θ) [x·secθ − θ·secx] / (x−θ) ═══════════
Step 1: Let x = θ+h, so h→0 as x→θ.
Step 2: lim(h→0) [(θ+h)secθ − θsec(θ+h)]/h = lim(h→0) θ[secθ−sec(θ+h)]/h + secθ
Step 3: Apply identity secA−secB = [cosB−cosA]/(cosA·cosB): secθ−sec(θ+h) = [cos(θ+h)−cosθ]/[cosθ·cos(θ+h)]
Step 4: Apply cosA−cosB identity to the numerator: cos(θ+h)−cosθ = −2·sin((2θ+h)/2)·sin(h/2)
Step 5: θ[secθ−sec(θ+h)]/h = −θ·2sin((2θ+h)/2)·sin(h/2) / [h·cosθ·cos(θ+h)] = −θ·sin((2θ+h)/2)·[sin(h/2)/(h/2)] / [cosθ·cos(θ+h)]
Step 6: As h→0: this term → −θ·sinθ / [cosθ·cosθ] = −θ·sinθ/cos²θ
Step 7: Add secθ = 1/cosθ: Total = −θsinθ/cos²θ + 1/cosθ = [cosθ − θsinθ]/cos²θ
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→θ) [x·secθ − θ·secx]/(x−θ) = (cosθ − θ·sinθ)/cos²θ = secθ·(1 − θ·tanθ)
Step 1: Let x − a = h, so h→0 as x→a, i.e., x = a+h.
Step 2: lim(h→0) [cot(a+h) − cota]/h
Step 3: Apply identity cotA−cotB = sin(B−A)/(sinA·sinB) with A=(a+h), B=a: cot(a+h)−cota = sin(a−(a+h))/[sin(a+h)·sina] = sin(−h)/[sin(a+h)sina] = −sinh/[sin(a+h)sina]
Step 4: Divide by h: [cot(a+h)−cota]/h = −[sinh/h]/[sin(a+h)·sina]
Step 5: As h→0: sinh/h→1, sin(a+h)→sina. This becomes: −1/[sina·sina] = −1/sin²a
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→a) [cotx − cota]/(x−a) = −1/sin²a = −cosec²a
═══════════ PROBLEM 7: lim(x→1) [1 + cos(πx)] / tan²(πx)   [algebraic-trig 0/0 form] ═══════════
Step 1: Direct substitution: x=1 → [1+cos(π)]/tan²(π) = [1+(−1)]/0 = 0/0 → INDETERMINATE, must simplify.
Step 2: Rewrite tan²(πx) = sin²(πx)/cos²(πx), so the expression = [1+cos(πx)]·cos²(πx) / sin²(πx)
Step 3: Use identity sin²(πx) = 1 − cos²(πx) = (1−cos(πx))(1+cos(πx))
Step 4: Substitute: = [1+cos(πx)]·cos²(πx) / [(1−cos(πx))(1+cos(πx))]
Step 5: Cancel the common factor (1+cos(πx)) from numerator and denominator: = cos²(πx)/(1−cos(πx))
Step 6: Now substitute x=1 directly (no longer 0/0): cos(π)=−1, so cos²(π)=1, and 1−cos(π)=1−(−1)=2
Step 7: = 1/2
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→1) [1+cos(πx)]/tan²(πx) = 1/2
Step 1: Let x − π/4 = h, so h→0 as x→π/4, i.e., x = π/4 + h.
Step 2: lim(h→0) [sin(π/4+h) − cos(π/4+h)]/h
Step 3: Expand using angle-sum formulas: sin(π/4+h) = sin(π/4)cosh + cos(π/4)sinh = (1/√2)cosh + (1/√2)sinh  ;  cos(π/4+h) = cos(π/4)cosh − sin(π/4)sinh = (1/√2)cosh − (1/√2)sinh
Step 4: Subtract: sin(π/4+h) − cos(π/4+h) = [(1/√2)cosh+(1/√2)sinh] − [(1/√2)cosh−(1/√2)sinh] = (2/√2)sinh = √2·sinh
Step 5: So the limit becomes: lim(h→0) √2·sinh / h = √2 · lim(h→0) [sinh/h]
Step 6: Apply the standard result lim(h→0) sinh/h = 1
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→π/4) (sinx − cosx)/(x − π/4) = √2
Step 1: Simplify cotx−tanx first using cotx = cosx/sinx and tanx = sinx/cosx: cotx−tanx = (cos²x−sin²x)/(sinx·cosx) = cos(2x)/[(1/2)sin(2x)] = 2·cos(2x)/sin(2x) = 2·cot(2x)
Step 2: The limit becomes: lim(x→π/4) 2cot(2x)/(x−π/4)
Step 3: Let x = π/4 + h, so h→0, and 2x = π/2 + 2h
Step 4: cot(π/2+2h) = −tan(2h)  (using the co-function shift identity cot(π/2+θ) = −tanθ)
Step 5: So 2cot(2x) = −2tan(2h), and (x−π/4) = h. The limit becomes: lim(h→0) −2tan(2h)/h
Step 6: Rewrite as: lim(h→0) −4·[tan(2h)/(2h)]
Step 7: Apply the standard result lim(θ→0) tanθ/θ = 1, with θ=2h: [tan(2h)/(2h)] → 1
✅ ANSWER: lim(x→π/4) (cotx − tanx)/(x − π/4) = −4

🎯 QUICK-REFERENCE SUMMARY OF ALL RESULTS: (1) [x sinθ−θ sinx]/(x−θ) → sinθ−θcosθ.

(2) [x cosθ−θ cosx]/(x−θ) → cosθ+θsinθ.

(3) [x tanθ−θ tanx]/(x−θ) → tanθ−θsec²θ.

(4) [x cosecθ−θ cosecx]/(x−θ) → cosecθ(1+θcotθ).

(5) [x secθ−θ secx]/(x−θ) → secθ(1−θtanθ).

(6) [cotx−cota]/(x−a) → −cosec²a.

(7) [1+cos(πx)]/tan²(πx) at x→1 → 1/2. (8) (sinx−cosx)/(x−π/4) at x→π/4 → √2. (9) (cotx−tanx)/(x−π/4) at x→π/4 → −4.

💡 PATTERN RECOGNITION TIP: Whenever you see the form [x·f(θ) − θ·f(x)]/(x−θ), ALWAYS substitute x = θ+h first — this is the standard opening move.

The problem then reduces to a limit of the form θ·[f(θ)−f(θ+h)]/h + f(θ), and you only need to know the correct sum-to-product identity for f(θ)−f(θ+h) to finish it off using lim(h→0) sin(h/2)/(h/2) = 1.

⚠️ IMPORTANT: These results resemble what you get from DIFFERENTIATION (first-principle definition of a derivative), since [x·f(θ)−θ·f(x)]/(x−θ) as x→θ is closely related to f(θ) − θ·f'(θ) pattern after rearrangement — this is why these problems are often given right before introducing derivatives, as a bridge topic connecting limits to calculus.
